questions.q: List the three discussion topics given in the NCERT textbook under "Talking About the Text" for "The Adventure of the Three Garridebs".
questions.a: The three topics are: (1) The Holmes-Watson relationship as revealed by the "cold mask" quote, (2) Whether clever criminals leave clues, (3) How Holmes's digressions prove relevant. A wrong answer (e.g., listing comprehension questions) reveals the student hasn't distinguished between literal comprehension questions and open-ended discussion prompts that require interpretation.

questions.q: In your own words, explain what the first discussion topic means by "cold mask" and why the wound is "worth many wounds".
questions.a: "Cold mask" refers to Holmes's habitual emotional detachment and analytical demeanor; the wound is "worth many wounds" because Watson's injury forces Holmes to momentarily drop this mask, revealing profound loyalty and love. A wrong answer focusing only on the physical wound reveals the student misses the metaphorical contrast between Holmes's professional persona and his private humanity.

questions.q: Using the text, identify two specific "digressions" Holmes makes during his interview with John Garrideb (the American lawyer) and explain what each digression reveals about the visitor.
questions.a: Digression 1: Holmes comments on Garrideb's English coat and boots, revealing the visitor has lived in London long-term despite claiming recent arrival. Digression 2: Holmes mentions Dr Lysander Starr of Topeka, testing Garrideb's reaction to a fabricated person, revealing the visitor's willingness to lie. A wrong answer listing only plot events shows the student cannot distinguish strategic digressions from narrative progression.

questions.q: Compare the three discussion topics in terms of their focus: which focuses on character relationship, which on criminal psychology, and which on narrative technique? Justify your categorization.
questions.a: Topic 1 focuses on character relationship (Holmes-Watson bond). Topic 2 focuses on criminal psychology (Killer Evans's clue-leaving). Topic 3 focuses on narrative technique (Doyle's use of digressions as plot device). A wrong answer that categorizes Topic 2 as narrative technique reveals confusion between authorial craft and in-story criminal behavior.

questions.q: Evaluate which of the three discussion topics would generate the most productive 10-minute group discussion for Class 11 students. Provide two criteria for your judgment.
questions.a: Topic 1 (Holmes-Watson relationship) would be most productive because: (a) it has abundant textual evidence across the story, allowing multiple entry points, and (b) it connects to universal themes of friendship and emotional vulnerability that resonate with adolescents. A wrong answer choosing Topic 2 because "it's about crime" reveals a preference for sensational content over literary depth.

questions.q: Create a fourth discussion topic for this story that would deepen understanding of a theme not covered by the existing three. Write the prompt exactly as it would appear in the textbook.
questions.a: "Examine how the story uses the 'three Garridebs' premise to explore the theme of identity and deception. Discuss with reference to Nathan Garrideb's collection, John Garrideb's disguise, and Holmes's detective persona." A poor answer that merely asks "Why are there three Garridebs?" reveals inability to frame an interpretive question that requires analysis rather than plot recall.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Speaking and Listening: Discussion Points refers to the structured oral communication skill where students ______ explore interpretive questions about a literary text, using textual evidence to support arguments, actively listening to peers, and building on ideas to develop deeper collective understanding.
Fill in the blank: Imagine your book club is meeting to discuss a Sherlock Holmes story where the ______ gets shot protecting his friend.
What is Speaking and Listening? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Speaking and Listening: Discussion Points refers to the structured oral communication skill where students collaboratively explore interpretive questions about a literary text, using textual evidence to support arguments, actively listening to peers, and building on ideas to develop deeper collective understanding.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Speaking and Listening?
questions.a: Students believe a literary discussion is a series of individual speeches where each person states their opinion.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can participate in a 10-minute group discussion on all three NCERT discussion topics, contributing at least two evidence-based points per topic, paraphrasing a peer's idea before responding, and synthesizing the group's conclusions in a closing statement.
